narrative: Crews of two B-17 Flying Fortresses from the 385th Bomb Group were flying a wartime mission from their base at Great Ashfield when the two aircraft collided in mid-air over Reedham Marshes, Norfolk, on 21 February 1944. Commander John Hutchison led one aircraft; Commander Warren Pease, of the 449th Bomber Squadron, commanded the other. The collision proved catastrophic: 21 of the 22 airmen aboard both aircraft were killed. Among those lost were William Gill Jr and John Terrace. Only one man survived the disaster.
community_connection: The story is connected to a memorial dedicated to these bombers and their crews.

events.name: Diversionary Raid on Diepholz Aircraft Depot
events.description: 34 aircraft from the 385th Bomber Group, 4th Bombardment Wing, 8th Air Force carried out a raid on Diepholz aircraft depot in N.W. Germany while the main force attacked an aircraft components works at Brunswick in Lower Saxony.
